components.label: Election gate
components.responsibility: Persist votes and term; reject candidates whose logs are not sufficiently up to date.

components.label: Snapshot installer
components.responsibility: Install a checksummed snapshot with last included index/term, then append the suffix.

components.label: Externally fenced primary and backups
components.responsibility: Preserve this stable boundary while refining its ownership and contracts.

components.label: Primary writer
components.responsibility: Require a current monotonically increasing storage fence on every mutation.

components.label: Primary journal
components.responsibility: Own durable sequenced writes and client result receipts.

components.label: Synchronous backup
components.responsibility: For zero declared loss within the selected failure model, await a durable backup receipt before success.

components.label: Fence authority
components.responsibility: Issue monotonic fencing tokens and enforce them at the storage mutation boundary.

components.label: Promotion verifier
components.responsibility: Compare durable acknowledgement watermark and available log prefixes before selecting a survivor.

components.label: Read replica
components.responsibility: Carry a minimum LSN token and wait or route to primary when a replica is behind.

components.label: Snapshot catchup
components.responsibility: Rejoin as a follower under the new fence and restore verified snapshot plus journal suffix.

components.label: Failover ledger
components.responsibility: Retain request IDs, promotion decisions and acknowledged LSN boundary for client retry resolution.

requirements.text: Distinguish acknowledged durable writes, committed prefixes and lagging applied state.
Prevent stale leaders from committing after promotion and refuse unsafe minority writes.
Recover through a verified snapshot/log boundary without skipping acknowledged records.

problem.scope: Extend the canonical three-slot synthetic replica exercise with an authored safety discussion. Compare quorum-log consensus with externally fenced primary/backup recovery; the canonical simulation itself proves neither split-brain safety nor consensus.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

acceptanceCases.given: A former leader is isolated from a majority.
acceptanceCases.then: The old leader cannot commit a new write; implementation safety remains a specification.
acceptanceCases.when: A newer term elects another leader.

acceptanceCases.given: A follower installs snapshot through index 10.
acceptanceCases.then: Apply one ordered committed prefix and retain request deduplication.

evidence.testName: fence comparison and bounded committed suffix retain recovery boundary

acceptanceCases.given: Installed fence is 5 and snapshot index is 10.
acceptanceCases.then: Reject token 4, stop before uncommitted 13, and reject a suffix gap; this is not consensus proof.
acceptanceCases.when: Compare token 4 and replay contiguous committed suffix through 12.

guarantees: An acknowledgement names a persisted matching prefix.
A bare count without term/configuration is insufficient.
Read success requires appliedIndex at least the read barrier.
Timeout triggers an election, not proof that the old leader is dead.
Snapshot and suffix meet at one verified boundary.
A repeated command sequence returns its original committed result.
